title: A geometrically irreducible scheme surjects onto the Hilbert scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve] that is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $d\geq0$, and let $H$ be a $k$-scheme representing [def-pc-representable-functor] the functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor]. Then there exist a $k$-scheme $Y$, a proper morphism $q:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and a morphism $\pi:Y\to H$ such that $Y$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $\pi$ is surjective, and $\pi$ followed by $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ equals $q$.
